title: Strings essentials
summary: Immutability, equality, slicing and building strings without hidden quadratic costs.

questions.prompt: True or false: s1.equals(s2) compares the characters, while s1 == s2 checks whether both variables refer to the same String object.
What is the time complexity of building the string this way, in terms of n?
Complete the line so reversed holds s backwards.
Why prefer StringBuilder when appending inside a loop?
options: Strings are immutable, so += copies the whole string every time; StringBuilder appends to a growable buffer
StringBuilder is thread-safe and String isn't
StringBuilder stores each character in less memory
